Here is the Plan Fidelity review. I read the precomputed diff and ran `git log $(git merge-base HEAD main)..HEAD --oneline` (read-only). Per your read-only constraint, I did not write a `.tsv` file on disk; the TSV lines are in a fenced block at the end for you to save as the sidecar if needed.

1. **Important** · **risk-integration** · `larch-logs/implement/A64270EC-9031-4E64-8FD3-C8AF78B38A89/` (new tracked tree in diff) vs implementation plan Parts A–B and “Sibling .md updates” / verification  
   The plan only called for edits to `tally-plan-review.sh`, related design docs/tests, the three shell call sites for token vs timing ledger, and the four sibling `.md` files plus running checks and `test-tally-plan-review.sh`. Nothing in the plan or feature description asks to **commit** a concrete `/implement` run tree under `larch-logs/implement/…` (`manifest.json`, `plan-goals-test.md`, `plan-review-tally.json`). That is out-of-band scope: it bakes a specific run id, placeholder operator paths, and `issue_number: 2228` into the shipped plugin tree while the stated work is **#2220** symmetry. Downstream risk: noise in PR review, mistaken “canonical” log samples, and future confusion about whether `larch-logs/` is a supported committed surface. **Suggested fix:** Drop these paths from the branch (or move any needed fixtures under an explicit test fixture location with a plan-approved contract), and keep only the scripted/doc changes the plan enumerates.

2. **Nit** · **correctness** · `skills/design/scripts/tally-plan-review.sh` (flush failure handling) vs plan step A.3 “`|| { warning_flush; true; }`”  
   On `write-tally.sh` failure the implementation emits breadcrumbs/`larch_err` and appends `execution-issues.md`, which matches the intent (non-fatal, surfaced warning). The exact mechanism differs from the plan’s shorthand; behavior is still best-effort and non-blocking. **Suggested fix:** None required for fidelity; align naming/comments with the plan only if you want strict doc/script parity.

**Plan traceability (summary):** Part A (`flush_plan_review_batch`, counters, `write-tally.sh`, both eligible and zero-judge paths, docs, regression test), Part B (token-ledger before timing-ledger in `step2-implement.sh`, `review-and-fix.sh` round 1, `run-relevant-checks-captured.sh` step3/step6), and the four sibling `.md` updates all appear implemented in line with the plan’s intent. The only material plan-vs-branch gap is the extra committed `larch-logs/` run artifacts.

None worth listing; nothing else clearly pre-existing was isolated in the supplied diff context.

1. **Important** (`correctness`) — [`skills/design/scripts/tally-plan-review.sh:223-234`](skills/design/scripts/tally-plan-review.sh) vs [`skills/design/scripts/tally-plan-review.sh:258-268`](skills/design/scripts/tally-plan-review.sh): New `accepted_count` / `rejected_count` passed to `write-tally.sh` treat every in-scope finding with `result != accepted` as `rejected_count++`, including `neutral` and `exonerated`. The scoreboard awk on the same run splits those into separate columns (`neutral` vs `rejected`). A consumer comparing the emitted `plan-review-tally.json` counts to the markdown table will see inconsistent totals (e.g. many “neutral” rows but a large `rejected_count`). **Suggested fix:** Align counter semantics with the scoreboard (separate fields or increment `rejected_count` only when `result` is the strict rejected class, and add explicit fields for neutral/exonerated if the batch schema allows), or document in the batch contract that `rejected_count` means “not accepted” and rename in JSON if downstream expects “rejected votes only.”

2. **Latent** (`risk-integration`) — [`skills/design/scripts/tally-plan-review.sh:139-147`](skills/design/scripts/tally-plan-review.sh): Body assembly `{ cat "$tally_file" ... } > "$body_file" || return 0` discards redirection/write failures with no breadcrumb, no `execution-issues.md` append, and no distinction from “skip because SESSION_ENV unset.” **Scenario:** Full disk or unwritable `$DESIGN_TMPDIR` after a successful tally — operators get a complete local tally and KV lines but no parent `plan-review-tally` batch with no durable signal. **Suggested fix:** On non-zero status from the compound redirect, emit the same breadcrumb / append path used for `write-tally` failure (or at least `emit_breadcrumb` before `return`).

3. **Nit** (`architecture`) — [`skills/design/scripts/tally-plan-review.sh:166-170`](skills/design/scripts/tally-plan-review.sh): `append-execution-issue.sh` is only checked with `-x` inside the `write_tally` failure branch, so a missing/non-executable append helper silently drops the durable warning even when `write_tally` failed. **Suggested fix:** Hoist the `-x "$append_issue"` guard (or log when absent) alongside the other tool guards at the top of `flush_plan_review_batch`.

4. **Nit** (`risk-integration`) — New tree [`larch-logs/implement/A64270EC-9031-4E64-8FD3-C8AF78B38A89/`](larch-logs/implement/A64270EC-9031-4E64-8FD3-C8AF78B38A89/) (second commit): Adds another full run-shaped fixture (large `plan-goals-test.md`, `manifest.json`, `plan-review-tally.json` in `simple` mode) that is not required to implement or test the new shell logic (the regression lives in `test-tally-plan-review.sh`). **Suggested fix:** Drop the extra committed fixture from this PR unless a maintainer explicitly wants that UUID in the golden corpus.

1. **Latent** (`risk-integration` / `plan`) — [`skills/design/scripts/tally-plan-review.sh:223-235`](skills/design/scripts/tally-plan-review.sh): `rejected_count` increments on the `else` branch for every in-scope finding where `result != "accepted"`, so `neutral` and `exonerated` outcomes are counted the same as true `rejected` tallies in the JSON sent to `write-tally.sh`. **Concrete scenario:** A finding that the panel exonerates or marks neutral still bumps `rejected_count`, so dashboards or batch consumers that treat `rejected_count` as “NO/rejected votes” misreport those runs versus the scoreboard columns that split Neutral/Exon from Rejected. **Suggested fix:** Either narrow increments to results classified as rejected only (if the schema allows), or add separate counter fields / document in `tally-plan-review.md` and the batch schema that `rejected_count` means “not accepted” (accepted vs non-accepted).

2. **Latent** (`security` / `plan`) — [`skills/design/scripts/tally-plan-review.sh:163-170`](skills/design/scripts/tally-plan-review.sh): On `write-tally.sh` failure, raw `tally_out` is interpolated into `append-execution-issue.sh --entry`, which is then written into `execution-issues.md`. **Concrete scenario:** If `write-tally` / `larch-log` ever prints stderr containing tmpdir paths, internal URLs, or other session-derived material, that string is persisted in the markdown audit trail without the redaction pass called out in `skills/implement/SKILL.md` for session-derived outbound text. **Suggested fix:** Pipe through the same redaction helper used elsewhere, truncate to a safe max size, or write a fixed token plus `entry-file` pointing at a redacted temp file.

3. **Nit** (`risk-integration` / `plan`) — [`skills/design/scripts/test-tally-plan-review.sh:232-235`](skills/design/scripts/test-tally-plan-review.sh): The new regression requires `jq` but the harness does not fail fast with a clear message if `jq` is missing (unlike `review-and-fix.sh`, which requires `jq` explicitly). **Suggested fix:** Add `command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "jq is required for plan-review-tally batch assertions"` near the top of the harness.

4. **Nit** (`risk-integration` / `requirements`) — [`larch-logs/implement/A64270EC-9031-4E64-8FD3-C8AF78B38A89/manifest.json`](larch-logs/implement/A64270EC-9031-4E64-8FD3-C8AF78B38A89/manifest.json): The committed run manifest sets `"issue_number": 2228` while the feature description references **#2220**, which makes committed run metadata harder to correlate with the stated symmetry issue. **Suggested fix:** Regenerate or edit the fixture so `issue_number` matches the tracking issue you want this run to represent (or document why 2228 is intentional).

5. **Nit** (`risk-integration` / `plan`) — [`skills/implement/scripts/step2-implement.sh:202-203`](skills/implement/scripts/step2-implement.sh), [`skills/review-and-fix/scripts/review-and-fix.sh:649-651`](skills/review-and-fix/scripts/review-and-fix.sh), [`scripts/run-relevant-checks-captured.sh:183-189`](scripts/run-relevant-checks-captured.sh): Part B only adds production calls; there is no new shell harness asserting that `token-ledger.sh mark` actually appends under the expected `IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR` (contrast with Part A’s `test-tally-plan-review.sh` extension). **Impact:** Syntax is still covered by agent-lint, but a regression in env wiring for `token-ledger` would not be caught until runtime. **Suggested fix:** Optionally extend an existing lightweight script test (e.g. step2-dispatch or relevant-checks validation) with a mocked tmpdir and a grep/jq check on the token ledger artifact.

1. **Nit** (`architecture`) — The repo already tracks a large tree under [`larch-logs/implement/`](larch-logs/implement/); adding another UUID directory is consistent with that pattern and is not by itself a regression introduced by this symmetry work (only the new run’s metadata mismatch is in-scope above).

1. **Important** (`code-quality`, `plan`) — [`skills/design/scripts/tally-plan-review.sh:139-147`](skills/design/scripts/tally-plan-review.sh) — The body assembly block ends with `} > "$body_file" || return 0`, so any failure creating or writing `plan-review-tally-body.md` exits `flush_plan_review_batch` silently: the HARD-path symmetry can be missing from `larch-logs` with no `execution-issues.md` entry and no breadcrumb, while local tally markdown still looks successful. Treat redirect/compose failure like `write_tally` failure (emit breadcrumb, optional `append-execution-issue`, or at least a non-silent diagnostic) instead of swallowing the error.

2. **Nit** (`architecture`) — [`skills/design/scripts/tally-plan-review.sh:167-170`](skills/design/scripts/tally-plan-review.sh) — The `append-execution-issue.sh` entry concatenates full `tally_out` from `write-tally.sh` into a single `--entry` string. Unbounded or multiline diagnostics can bloat `execution-issues.md` or break markdown layout. Cap length and normalize newlines (reuse patterns from other appenders if any exist).

3. **Latent** (`code-quality`, `plan`) — [`skills/design/scripts/tally-plan-review.md:34`](skills/design/scripts/tally-plan-review.md) and counter logic at [`skills/design/scripts/tally-plan-review.sh:223-235`](skills/design/scripts/tally-plan-review.sh) — `rejected_count` increments for every in-scope finding whose `classify_result` is not `accepted`, so neutral and exonerated outcomes are counted in `rejected_count` even though the scoreboard treats them separately. A consumer interpreting `rejected_count` as “NO-vote rejections only” will misread panels heavy in neutral/exonerated results. Clarify in the contract that the JSON field means “not accepted” (or split counters if downstream needs vote-outcome fidelity).

4. **Nit** (`code-quality`) — [`skills/implement/scripts/step2-implement.sh:202-203`](skills/implement/scripts/step2-implement.sh) vs [`skills/review-and-fix/scripts/review-and-fix.sh:649-651`](skills/review-and-fix/scripts/review-and-fix.sh) / [`scripts/run-relevant-checks-captured.sh:183-189`](scripts/run-relevant-checks-captured.sh) — Step 2 relies on the already-exported `IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR`, while the other two sites pass `IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR="$IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR"` explicitly on the helper invocation. Behavior matches, but the style is inconsistent and slightly weaker if a future edit moves the marks before the export. Prefer one consistent pattern (either always prefix the subprocess env or always rely on export).
